title: The green one is prettier — comparing
title_target: हरा वाला ज़्यादा सुंदर है — haraa vaalaa zyaadaa sundar hai
goal: Compare two things and name the "most" — while buying clothes, naming colors, and using one little suffix that makes your Hindi sound far more natural: वाला.
bekal: naming colors and making them agree

dialogs.title: संवाद — Choosing a kurta
dialogs.intro: Ani is buying clothes. Look at lines four and eight: Hindi compares two things without a special word for "more" — just से in the right place.

lines.speaker: दुकानदार:
lines.id: Yes, ma'am, what would you like?

lines.speaker: दुकानदार:
lines.id: Have a look at this — the blue one.

lines.speaker: आनी:
lines.id: The blue one is nice, but the green one is prettier.
lines.literal: blue — nice — is, but — green — one — more — beautiful — is.

lines.speaker: दुकानदार:
lines.id: The green one is a bit more expensive.

lines.speaker: दुकानदार:
lines.id: The blue one is eight hundred, the green one twelve hundred.
lines.literal: blue — eight — hundred, green — twelve — hundred.

lines.speaker: आनी:
lines.id: The green one is four hundred more than the blue one!
lines.literal: green — blue(obl.) — than — four — hundred — more — is!

lines.speaker: दुकानदार:
lines.id: Yes, but the fabric is better. It's the finest we have.
lines.literal: yes, but — fabric — better — is. of-all — good — goods — is.

lines.speaker: आनी:
lines.id: Do you have a smaller size? This looks a bit big.
lines.literal: small — size — is? this — a-little — big — seem — -ing — is.

lines.speaker: दुकानदार:
lines.id: Yes, ma'am. Try it on — the fitting room is over there.
lines.literal: is — ji. after-wearing — look, there — room — is.

lines.speaker: आनी:
lines.id: Okay. If it fits, I'll take it.
lines.literal: good — is. if — fit — happens — then — take — will-take(fem.).

notes: **Comparing needs no word for "more" — just से.** *हरा नीले **से** महँगा है* = "the green one is more expensive than the blue one". Literally "green from blue expensive". ⚠️ Notice that the thing compared with comes **second** and takes से, and that नीला goes into the oblique form **नीले** because से follows it.

**You can add ज़्यादा, but you don't have to.** *हरा नीले से ज़्यादा महँगा है* and *हरा नीले से महँगा है* are both correct and both common. Adding ज़्यादा makes the comparison sharper. For the other direction, use **कम**: *यह उससे कम महँगा है* (this is less expensive than that).

**"Most" is formed with सबसे — literally "than all".** *सबसे अच्छा* (the best), *सबसे बड़ा* (the biggest), *सबसे सस्ता* (the cheapest), *सबसे छोटी बहन* (the youngest sister). ⚠️ The structure is exactly the same as an ordinary comparison; the thing compared with is just replaced by "all".

**A few adjectives have their own comparative forms from Persian — and you can use them as they are.** **अच्छा → बेहतर** (better) **→ बेहतरीन** (best). **ख़राब → बदतर** (worse). ⚠️ These words already contain "more", so don't add ज़्यादा: *ज़्यादा बेहतर* sounds redundant, just like "more better".

**वाला — the suffix that makes you sound natural.** You met it in Unit 11 (*ऑटो वाला*). Here it has a different job: it means "the … **one**". **नीला वाला** (the blue one), **बड़ा वाला** (the big one), **वो वाला** (that one), **सस्ते वाले** (the cheap ones). In everyday shopping, वाला is used constantly, and using it even once changes how your sentence sounds.

**लग रहा है = "it looks, it seems".** *यह बड़ा लग रहा है* (this looks too big), *अच्छा लग रहा है* (it looks good), *मुझे ठीक लग रहा है* (it seems fine to me). You've met the verb **लगना** in Units 8, 13 and 16 with different meanings — to stick, to take (time), to feel. ⚠️ It's one of the most versatile verbs in Hindi, and its meaning is always set by the sentence pattern.

**Colors ending in -आ change form; the rest don't.** **लाल** (red), **हरा** (green), **नीला** (blue), **पीला** (yellow), **काला** (black), **सफ़ेद** (white), **भूरा** (brown), **गुलाबी** (pink), **नारंगी** (orange). Only हरा, नीला, पीला, काला, भूरा change — *हरी साड़ी*, *काली गाड़ी*. लाल, सफ़ेद, गुलाबी, नारंगी stay the same. ⚠️ **गुलाबी** comes from **गुलाब** (rose) and **नारंगी** from **नारंगी** (orange, the fruit) — exactly like English "orange", the fruit and the color.

grammars.title: Comparing
after: ⚠️ Notice that **छोटा** appears twice: it means "small" and also "short" for people. For short things, **छोटा** is used too; for tall people, **लंबा**.

grammars.title: Colors and clothes
after: Clothes-shopping sentences: **यह मुझे फ़िट नहीं है** (this doesn't fit me), **बड़ा साइज़ है?** (do you have a bigger size?), **दूसरा रंग है?** (is there another color?), **पहनकर देख सकती हूँ?** (can I try it on?), **यह कपड़ा क्या है?** (what fabric is this?).

blocks.text: A few things worth knowing before you walk into a fabric shop or clothing market in India — places that, for many visitors, become one of the happiest memories of the trip.

items: **Shops with price tags don't bargain; fabric shops and market stalls do.** Same rule as in Unit 6.

**In a fabric shop, you'll be seated and offered tea**, and then the shelves will be emptied in front of you, one bolt at a time. It's custom, not pressure; you can leave without buying and no one will be offended — though it's nice to thank them sincerely.

**कुर्ता is worn by men and women alike**, comfortable in hot weather, and a safe choice for modest dress in most places. Women often wear it with a **दुपट्टा** — a long scarf that's also handy for covering your head when entering a place of worship.
**Shoes come off** before entering homes, temples, mosques and many small shops. Slip-on sandals are far more practical than lace-up shoes.

⚠️ **Colors carry meaning in some situations.** Red and bright colors are linked to celebrations and weddings; plain white is linked to mourning in Hindu custom. It's not a rule for foreign guests, but knowing it saves you from a wrong choice at an important event.

blocks.title: Six sentences you'll use
items: **यह कितने का है?** — How much is this?
**दूसरा रंग है?** — Is there another color?
**बड़ा साइज़ दिखाइए।** — Show me a bigger size, please.
**पहनकर देख सकती हूँ?** — Can I try it on?
**थोड़ा कम कीजिए।** — Bring the price down a little.
**सोचकर आती हूँ।** — I'll think about it and come back. ⚠️ The gentlest way to leave a shop without buying — and it often makes the price drop just before you reach the door.

blocks.text: One last word about **वाला**, because it really deserves your attention. This suffix is used everywhere and almost always makes a sentence sound more alive: *लाल वाला दीजिए* (give me the red one), *कल वाली बात* (yesterday's matter), *आने वाली ट्रेन* (the incoming train), *बाद वाला* (the later one), *पहले वाला* (the earlier one). ⚠️ It's even used to say something is about to happen: *ट्रेन आने वाली है* = "the train is about to arrive". One suffix, dozens of uses — and none of them hard.
